jit_precompile_functions.name: jit_precompile_functions
jit_precompile_functions.description: Comma-separated guest function addresses (hex) to compile when the title loads, before its first thread runs. For titles whose non-thread-safe static initialization sets its guard before calling a constructor: the first call compiles the constructor, which widens a nanosecond race into milliseconds (Ultra Street Fighter IV's boot crash).

time_scalar.name: time_scalar
time_scalar.description: Scalar used to speed or slow time (1x, 2x, 1/2x, etc).

launch_module.name: launch_module
launch_module.description: Executable to launch from the .iso or the package instead of default.xex or the module specified by the game. Leave blank to launch the default module.

allow_game_relative_writes.name: allow_game_relative_writes
allow_game_relative_writes.description: Not useful to non-developers. Allows code to write to paths relative to game://. Used for generating test data to compare with original hardware.

priority_class.name: priority_class
priority_class.description: Forces Xenia to use different process priority than default one. It might affect performance and cause unexpected bugs. Possible values: 0 - Normal, 1 - Above normal, 2 - High

protect_zero.name: protect_zero
protect_zero.description: Protect the zero page from reads and writes.

emit_inline_mmio_checks.name: emit_inline_mmio_checks
emit_inline_mmio_checks.description: Emit inline MMIO range checks for all I32 loads/stores instead of relying on exception-based MMIO detection.

emit_mmio_aware_stores_for_recorded_exce.name: emit_mmio_aware_stores_for_recorded_exception_addresses
emit_mmio_aware_stores_for_recorded_exce.description: Uses info gathered via record_mmio_access_exceptions to emit special stores that are faster than trapping the exception

record_mmio_access_exceptions.name: record_mmio_access_exceptions
record_mmio_access_exceptions.description: For guest addresses records whether we caught any mmio accesses for them. This info can then be used on a subsequent run to instruct the recompiler to emit checks

protect_on_release.name: protect_on_release
protect_on_release.description: Protect released memory to prevent accesses.

scribble_heap.name: scribble_heap
scribble_heap.description: Scribble specific or random value into all allocated heap memory.

scribble_heap_value.name: scribble_heap_value
scribble_heap_value.description: Value used to fill all allocated heap memory. 0 - Random value. Valid range: [1-255]

defaults_date.name: defaults_date
defaults_date.description: Do not modify - internal version of the default values in the config, for seamless updates if default value of any option is changed.

notification_sound_path.name: notification_sound_path
notification_sound_path.description: Path (including filename) to selected notification sound. Sound MUST be in wav format!

custom_font_path.name: custom_font_path
custom_font_path.description: Allows user to load custom font and use it instead of default one.

font_size.name: font_size
font_size.description: Allows user to set custom font size.

check_for_updates.name: check_for_updates
check_for_updates.description: When to look on macxenos.com for a newer macXenos (Sparkle): launch (each time the app starts), weekly, monthly or never. It offers the update and installs nothing without asking. Checking by hand from the app menu works whatever this is.

check_for_updates_asked.name: check_for_updates_asked
check_for_updates_asked.description: Whether the first-launch question about update checks has been answered. Until it is, the app does not look for updates on its own.

host_present_from_non_ui_thread.name: host_present_from_non_ui_thread
host_present_from_non_ui_thread.description: Allow the GPU emulation thread to present the guest output to the host surface directly instead of requesting the UI thread to do so through the host window system.

present_render_pass_clear.name: present_render_pass_clear
present_render_pass_clear.description: On graphics backends where this is supported, use the clear render pass load operation in presentation instead of clear commands clearing only the letterbox area.

present_letterbox.name: present_letterbox
present_letterbox.description: Maintain aspect ratio when stretching by displaying bars around the image when there's no more overscan area to crop out.

present_safe_area_x.name: present_safe_area_x
present_safe_area_x.description: Percentage of the image width that can be kept when presenting to maintain aspect ratio without letterboxing or stretching.

present_safe_area_y.name: present_safe_area_y
present_safe_area_y.description: Percentage of the image height that can be kept when presenting to maintain aspect ratio without letterboxing or stretching.

window_guest_resolution_mode.name: window_guest_resolution_mode
window_guest_resolution_mode.description: How the window is sized from the guest resolution when a title launches: 'scaled' (window logical/point size equals the guest resolution; on a HiDPI display the backing store is larger by the scale factor), 'actual' (window physical pixel size equals the guest resolution - true 1:1, a smaller window on HiDPI), or 'off' (keep the window_size_x/y size). Currently implemented on macOS only.

metal_fsr_half_precision.name: metal_fsr_half_precision
metal_fsr_half_precision.description: Run AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) in half precision (16 bits) on the Metal renderer: 11-12% less GPU time at 4K and 5K output on an M4, with no visible difference. Takes effect on the next launch.

vulkan_log_debug_messages.name: vulkan_log_debug_messages
vulkan_log_debug_messages.description: Write Vulkan VK_EXT_debug_utils messages to the Xenia log, as opposed to the OS debug output.

mvk_config_defaults.name: mvk_config_defaults
mvk_config_defaults.description: Apply a curated set of MoltenVK MVK_CONFIG_* translation-layer defaults before instance creation (e.g. recover from transient Metal command-buffer errors instead of losing the device). Each knob is only set if the same environment variable is not already present, so a user-provided value always wins. Set to false to let MoltenVK run on its own defaults (for regression bisection). Does not change rendering output (no resolution scaling, no anti-aliasing).

mvk_metal_argument_buffers.name: mvk_metal_argument_buffers
mvk_metal_argument_buffers.description: On Apple GPUs, enable MoltenVK Metal argument buffers (MVK_CONFIG_USE_METAL_ARGUMENT_BUFFERS=1) by default. Lowers per-draw descriptor overhead - measured ~10% higher in-fight fps in USF4 on M4 (~44 -> ~48-51). Part of the curated mvk_config_defaults set; an explicit MVK_CONFIG_USE_METAL_ARGUMENT_BUFFERS in the environment still wins. Set to false if a title shows descriptor-related visual corruption - argument buffers change Metal descriptor handling and can glitch on some content.

vulkan_validation.name: vulkan_validation
vulkan_validation.description: Enable the Vulkan validation layer (VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation). Messages will be written to the Xenia log if 'vulkan_log_debug_messages' is enabled, or to the OS debug output otherwise.

vulkan_device.name: vulkan_device
vulkan_device.description: Index of the preferred Vulkan physical device, or -1 to use any compatible device.

vulkan_allow_present_mode_immediate.name: vulkan_allow_present_mode_immediate
vulkan_allow_present_mode_immediate.description: When available, allow the immediate presentation mode (1st priority), offering the lowest latency with the possibility of tearing in certain cases, and, depending on the configuration, variable refresh rate.

vulkan_allow_present_mode_mailbox.name: vulkan_allow_present_mode_mailbox
vulkan_allow_present_mode_mailbox.description: When available, allow the mailbox presentation mode (2nd priority), offering low latency without the possibility of tearing.

vulkan_allow_present_mode_fifo_relaxed.name: vulkan_allow_present_mode_fifo_relaxed
vulkan_allow_present_mode_fifo_relaxed.description: When available, allow the relaxed first-in-first-out presentation mode (3rd priority), which causes waiting for host display vertical sync, but may present with tearing if frames don't meet the host display refresh rate.

vulkan_semaphore_reuse_workaround.name: vulkan_semaphore_reuse_workaround
vulkan_semaphore_reuse_workaround.description: Wait for presentation queue idle before each frame to prevent semaphore reuse. May fix rendering issues but causes significant performance loss.

execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu.name: execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu
execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu.description:
Execute the vertex shader for draws with clipping disabled, primarily screen-space draws (such as clears), on the CPU when possible to estimate the extent of the EDRAM involved in the draw.
Enabling this may significantly improve GPU performance as otherwise up to the entire EDRAM may be considered used in draws without clipping, potentially resulting in spurious EDRAM range ownership transfer round trips between host render targets.
Also, on hosts where certain render target formats have to be emulated in a lossy way (for instance, 16-bit fixed-point via 16-bit floating-point), this prevents corruption of other render targets located after the current ones in the EDRAM by lossy range ownership transfers done for those draws.

execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu_with_sc.name: execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu_with_scissor
execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu_with_sc.description:
Don't restrict the usage of execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu to only non-scissored draws (with the right and the bottom sides of the scissor rectangle at 8192 or beyond) even though if the scissor rectangle is present, it's usually sufficient for esimating the height of the render target.
Enabling this may cause excessive processing of vertices on the CPU, as some games draw rectangles (for their UI, for instance) without clipping, but with a proper scissor rectangle.

depth_transfer_not_equal_test.name: depth_transfer_not_equal_test
depth_transfer_not_equal_test.description:
When transferring data between depth render targets, use the "not equal" test to avoid writing rewriting depth via shader depth output if it's the same as the one currently in the depth buffer in case of round trips of the data.
Settings this to true may make transfer round trips more friendly to depth compression depending on how the GPU implements it (as arbitrary depth output may result in it being disabled completely), which is beneficial to subsequent rendering, while setting this to false may reduce bandwidth usage during transfers as the previous depth won't need to be read.

depth_float24_round.name: depth_float24_round
depth_float24_round.description:
Whether to round to the nearest even, rather than truncating (rounding towards zero), the depth when converting it to 24-bit floating-point (20e4) from the host precision (32-bit floating point) when using a host depth buffer.
false:
 Recommended.
 The conversion may move the depth values farther away from the camera.
 Without depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader:
  The "greater or equal" depth test function continues to work fine if the full host precision depth data is lost, it's still possible to draw another pass of the same geometry with it.
  (See the description of depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader for more information about full precision depth data loss.)
 With depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader:
  Faster - the pixel shader for hidden surfaces may still be skipped (using conservative depth output).
true:
 Only for special cases of issues caused by minor 32-bit floating-point rounding errors, for instance, when the game tries to draw something at the camera plane by setting Z of the vertex position to W.
 The conversion may move the depth values closer or farther.
 Using the same rounding mode as in the Direct3D 9 reference rasterizer.
 Without depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader:
  Not possible to recover from a full host precision depth data loss - in subsequent passes of rendering the same geometry, half of the samples will be failing the depth test with the "greater or equal" depth test function.
 With depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader:
  Slower - depth rejection before the pixel shader is not possible.
When the depth buffer is emulated in software (via the fragment shader interlock / rasterizer-ordered view), this is ignored, and rounding to the nearest even is always done.

depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader.name: depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader
depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader.description:
Whether to convert the depth values to 24-bit floating-point (20e4) from the host precision (32-bit floating point) directly in the pixel shaders of guest draws when using a host depth buffer.
This prevents visual artifacts (interleaved stripes of parts of surfaces rendered and parts not rendered, having either the same width in case of the "greater or equal" depth test function, or the former being much thinner than the latter with the "equal" function) if the full host precision depth data is lost.
This issue may happen if the game reloads the depth data previously evicted from the EDRAM to the RAM back to the EDRAM, but the EDRAM region that previously contained that depth buffer was overwritten by another depth buffer, or the game loads it to a different location in the EDRAM than it was previously placed at, thus Xenia is unable to restore the depth data with the original precision, and instead falls back to converting the lower-precision values, so in subsequent rendering passes for the same geometry, the actual depth values of the surfaces don't match those stored in the depth buffer anymore.
This is a costly option because it makes the GPU unable to use depth buffer compression, and also with MSAA, forces the pixel shader to run for every subpixel sample rather than for the entire pixel, making pixel shading 2 or 4 times heavier depending on the MSAA sample count.
The rounding direction is controlled by the depth_float24_round configuration variable.
Note that with depth_float24_round = true, this becomes even more costly because pixel shaders must be executed regardless of whether the surface is behind the previously drawn surfaces. With depth_float24_round = false, conservative depth output is used, however, so depth rejection before the pixel shader may still work.
If sample-rate shading is not supported by the host GPU, the conversion in the pixel shader is done only when MSAA is not used.
When the depth buffer is emulated in software (via the fragment shader interlock / rasterizer-ordered view), this is ignored because 24-bit depth is always used directly.

depth_float24_convert_auto.name: depth_float24_convert_auto
depth_float24_convert_auto.description: Automatically enable depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader on hosts that lack a native 24-bit unorm depth format (notably Apple GPUs via MoltenVK, which fall back to 32-bit float depth). Without a native 24-bit format the guest depth prepass and color pass retain divergent low-order bits, so fragments fail the guest depth test along shared triangle edges, producing the cross-title "wireframe mesh" crack overlay. On such hosts this quantizes guest depth to 20e4 in the pixel shader so both passes agree. Hosts with a native 24-bit depth format are unaffected. Set to false to opt out of the automatic behavior (the escape hatch if it regresses a title); depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader=true still force-enables it everywhere regardless of this flag.

draw_resolution_scaled_texture_offsets.name: draw_resolution_scaled_texture_offsets
draw_resolution_scaled_texture_offsets.description: Apply offsets from texture fetch instructions taking resolution scale into account for render-to-texture, for more correct shadow filtering, bloom, etc., in some cases.

gamma_render_target_as_unorm16.name: gamma_render_target_as_unorm16
gamma_render_target_as_unorm16.description: When the host can't write 8 bits per component pixels with piecewise linear gamma encoding directly with correct blending, use the 16-bit unsigned normalized format, if supported, for conceptually correct 8_8_8_8_GAMMA render target format blending in linear color space. Greatly increases accuracy for this format, but may result in render target copying costs if the game switches between 8_8_8_8_GAMMA and 8_8_8_8 views for the same EDRAM render target.

mrt_edram_used_range_clamp_to_min.name: mrt_edram_used_range_clamp_to_min
mrt_edram_used_range_clamp_to_min.description:
With host render targets, if multiple render targets are bound, estimate the EDRAM range modified in any of them to be not bigger than the distance between any two render targets in the EDRAM, rather than allowing the last one claim the rest of the EDRAM.
Has effect primarily on draws without viewport clipping.
Setting this to false results in higher accuracy in rare cases, but may increase the amount of copying that needs to be done sometimes.

native_2x_msaa.name: native_2x_msaa
native_2x_msaa.description: Use host 2x MSAA when available. Can be disabled for scalability testing on host GPU APIs where 2x is not mandatory, in this case, 2 samples of 4x MSAA will be used instead (with similar or worse quality and higher memory usage).

native_stencil_value_output.name: native_stencil_value_output
native_stencil_value_output.description: Use pixel shader stencil reference output where available for purposes like copying between render targets. Can be disabled for scalability testing, in this case, much more expensive drawing of 8 quads will be done.

snorm16_render_target_full_range.name: snorm16_render_target_full_range
snorm16_render_target_full_range.description: When the host can only support 16_16 and 16_16_16_16 render targets as -1...1, remap -32...32 to -1...1 to use the full possible range of values, at the expense of multiplicative blending correctness.

execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu_for_psi.name: execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu_for_psi_render_backend
execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu_for_psi.description:
If execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu is enabled, execute the vertex shader for unclipped draws on the CPU even when using the pixel shader interlock (rasterizer-ordered view) implementation of the render backend on the host, for which no expensive copying between host render targets is needed when the ownership of a EDRAM range is changed.
If this is enabled, excessive barriers may be eliminated when switching between different render targets in separate EDRAM locations.

store_shaders.name: store_shaders
store_shaders.description: Store shaders persistently and load them when loading games to avoid runtime spikes and freezes when playing the game not for the first time.

texture_upload_log.name: texture_upload_log
texture_upload_log.description: Diagnostic: log every texture data upload with XXH3 hashes of the guest source ranges (base and mips). Diffing two identical replays' logs separates nondeterministic guest-source content from GPU-side upload/view races.

draw_resolution_scale_x.name: draw_resolution_scale_x
draw_resolution_scale_x.description:
Integer pixel width scale used for scaling the rendering resolution opaquely to the game.
Values from 1 to 7 may be supported, depending on device capabilities. Requires sparse binding (Vulkan) or tiled resources (D3D12) for scales above 1x1. The emulator will automatically clamp to the maximum supported scale if the requested value exceeds device limits.
Various effects and parts of game rendering pipelines may work incorrectly as pixels become ambiguous from the game's perspective and because half-pixel offset (which normally doesn't affect coverage when MSAA isn't used) becomes full-pixel.

draw_resolution_scale_y.name: draw_resolution_scale_y
draw_resolution_scale_y.description:
Integer pixel width scale used for scaling the rendering resolution opaquely to the game.
See draw_resolution_scale_x for more information.

texture_cache_memory_limit_soft.name: texture_cache_memory_limit_soft
texture_cache_memory_limit_soft.description: Maximum host texture memory usage (in megabytes) above which old textures will be destroyed.

texture_cache_memory_limit_soft_lifetime.name: texture_cache_memory_limit_soft_lifetime
texture_cache_memory_limit_soft_lifetime.description: Seconds a texture should be unused to be considered old enough to be deleted if texture memory usage exceeds texture_cache_memory_limit_soft.

texture_cache_memory_limit_hard.name: texture_cache_memory_limit_hard
texture_cache_memory_limit_hard.description: Maximum host texture memory usage (in megabytes) above which textures will be destroyed as soon as possible.

texture_cache_memory_limit_render_to_tex.name: texture_cache_memory_limit_render_to_texture
texture_cache_memory_limit_render_to_tex.description:
Part of the host texture memory budget (in megabytes) that will be scaled by the current drawing resolution scale.
If texture_cache_memory_limit_soft, for instance, is 384, and this is 24, it will be assumed that the game will be using roughly 24 MB of render-to-texture (resolve) targets and 384 - 24 = 360 MB of regular textures - so with 2x2 resolution scaling, the soft limit will be 360 + 96 MB, and with 3x3, it will be 360 + 216 MB.

tiled_shared_memory.name: tiled_shared_memory
tiled_shared_memory.description: Enable tiled/sparse resources for efficient large address space support. Disable for graphics debugger compatibility.

log_guest_driven_gpu_register_written_va.name: log_guest_driven_gpu_register_written_values
log_guest_driven_gpu_register_written_va.description: Only does anything in debug builds, if set will log every write to a gpu register done by a guest. Does not log writes that are done by the CP on its own, just ones the guest makes or instructs it to make.

disassemble_pm4.name: disassemble_pm4
disassemble_pm4.description: Only does anything in debug builds, if set will disassemble and log all PM4 packets sent to the CP.

log_fps.name: log_fps
log_fps.description: Log the guest frame rate (swap rate) every 5 seconds.

log_ringbuffer_kickoff_initiator_bts.name: log_ringbuffer_kickoff_initiator_bts
log_ringbuffer_kickoff_initiator_bts.description: Only does anything in debug builds, if set will log the pseudo-stacktrace of the guest thread that wrote the new read position.

clear_memory_page_state.name: clear_memory_page_state
clear_memory_page_state.description: Refresh state of memory pages to enable gpu written data. (Use for 'Team Ninja' Games to fix missing character models)

replay_draw_first.name: replay_draw_first
replay_draw_first.description: First draw index (inclusive, counted per trace playback) to actually issue to the backend. Draws outside [replay_draw_first, replay_draw_last] are skipped. For bisecting trace replays; no effect on live play at defaults.

replay_draw_last.name: replay_draw_last
replay_draw_last.description: Last draw index (inclusive) to actually issue to the backend during trace playback. See replay_draw_first.

replay_draw_include.name: replay_draw_include
replay_draw_include.description: Draw index that is always issued during trace playback even when outside [replay_draw_first, replay_draw_last] (e.g. the frame's final EDRAM resolve, so scene-window bisection still produces displayable output).

replay_draw_skip_first.name: replay_draw_skip_first
replay_draw_skip_first.description: First draw index (inclusive) of a range to SKIP during trace playback (in addition to the [first, last] window). -1 disables. For crack-creator bisection with intact exposure.

replay_draw_skip_last.name: replay_draw_skip_last
replay_draw_skip_last.description: Last draw index (inclusive) of the skip range. See replay_draw_skip_first.

replay_skip_depth_only.name: replay_skip_depth_only
replay_skip_depth_only.description: Skip kDepthOnly (Z-prepass) draws during trace playback - diagnostic for prepass-vs-color-pass depth mismatches.

replay_zfunc_always_draw.name: replay_zfunc_always_draw
replay_zfunc_always_draw.description: Draw index whose depth test function is forced to ALWAYS during trace playback (diagnostic: distinguishes depth-test failures from rasterization coverage gaps). -1 disables.

replay_index_window.name: replay_index_window
replay_index_window.description: draw,start,count - restrict one draw during trace playback to a window of its index buffer (diagnostic: isolate strip segments/triangles; count=0 skips the draw). Empty disables.

replay_solid_draw.name: replay_solid_draw
replay_solid_draw.description: Draw index whose RT0 blending is forced to REPLACE (src ONE, dst ZERO, ADD) and whose fixed-function alpha test / alpha-to-mask are disabled during trace playback (diagnostic: any pixel the draw rasterizes shows its raw fragment color, distinguishing absent fragments - cull/clip/coverage - from zero-alpha blend contributions). -1 disables.

replay_duplicate_draw_stencil.name: replay_duplicate_draw_stencil
replay_duplicate_draw_stencil.description: Draw index that is issued a SECOND time during trace playback with zfunc=LESS, depth writes off, and stencil REPLACE (ref 0xAB) on depth pass. Any sample whose re-rasterized depth is strictly below the just-written depth of the identical draw gets stencil-marked - a guest-visible detector of host fixed-function depth non-repeatability (diagnostic for the Apple wireframe-mesh hunt). -1 disables.

replay_duplicate_draw_depth_only.name: replay_duplicate_draw_depth_only
replay_duplicate_draw_depth_only.description: Make the second instance of replay_duplicate_draw_stencil run as a kDepthOnly (fragment-less, Z-prepass-like) draw, to test depth rasterization invariance BETWEEN pipeline variants of the same geometry rather than within one pipeline.

replay_draw_log.name: replay_draw_log
replay_draw_log.description: Log one line per draw (index, primitive, index count, EDRAM mode, shader ucode hashes) during trace playback bisection.

capture_dir.name: capture_dir
capture_dir.description: Headless trace-analysis capture directory. When set during trace playback, writes one structured JSON row per draw to <dir>/manifest.jsonl (byte-stable per-draw guest/register state for cross-machine and cross-build divergence compare) plus run/build/device provenance to <dir>/capture_meta.json. Empty disables (default output unchanged).

capture_draw_range.name: capture_draw_range
capture_draw_range.description: With --capture_dir: 'A..B' - snapshot raw EDRAM to <dir>/draw_NNNNNN.edram.bin AFTER each issued draw in the inclusive index range [A,B]. Selective and opt-in; the snapshot forces a submission + queue drain (NOT passive - may perturb, per design D3). Empty disables EDRAM snapshots.

capture_edram_at.name: capture_edram_at
capture_edram_at.description: With --capture_dir: comma-separated explicit draw indices (e.g. '101,108,115') to snapshot raw EDRAM after, in addition to any --capture_draw_range. Empty disables.

capture_edram_hashes.name: capture_edram_hashes
capture_edram_hashes.description: With --capture_dir: after EVERY draw, append per-tile, per-physical-sample-plane XXH3-64 hashes of the raw EDRAM image to <dir>/edram_hashes.bin (16-byte header: 'XEDH', version, tile_count, tile_bytes; then records of uint32 draw index + tile_count*4 uint64 hashes, little-endian). Sample planes use the canonical 32bpp 4x physical layout. Full-frame first-divergence scanning at ~64 KB/draw instead of 10 MB snapshots. Forces a submission + queue drain per draw (NOT passive, design D3).

serialize_draw_range.name: serialize_draw_range
serialize_draw_range.description: 'A..B' (inclusive): force a GPU submission + wait after each draw whose index is in the range, WITHOUT any capture output. Hazard-bisection probe: draws in the range execute against fully-drained GPU state, so corruption that disappears when a range is serialized implicates a GPU ordering hazard among those draws (tools/bisect_stipple.sh drives a binary search on this). Same draw-index space as --capture_draw_range. Empty disables.

replay_inject_memory.name: replay_inject_memory
replay_inject_memory.description: Trace-replay diagnostic: semicolon-separated list of hexaddr,afterdraw,filepath - before issuing draw index 'afterdraw', copy the file's contents into guest physical memory at hexaddr and invalidate caches (e.g. substitute another host's resolved shadow map for cross-GPU divergence attribution).

occlusion_query.name: occlusion_query
occlusion_query.description:
Controls hardware occlusion query behavior for EVENT_WRITE_ZPD.
Used for effects like lens flares, object culling, and auto-exposure.
 fake: Write a fake result without asking the GPU. Safe for most games,
       though some effects may look slightly wrong.
 fast: Ask the GPU but don't wait for the answer. Writes a cached
       result immediately and updates it when the GPU catches up.
       Cached results bias toward visible when guessing. (default)
 fast-alt: Variant of fast mode that keeps cached zero results for
           unresolved reports. May improve effects relying on precise
           visibility, but may be less stable for occlusion culling.
 strict: Ask the GPU and wait for the real result before continuing.
         Most accurate, but may be somewhat less performant.

readback_resolve.name: readback_resolve
readback_resolve.description:
Controls CPU readback of render-to-texture resolve results.
 fast: Read from previous frame (1 frame delay, no GPU stall, slight performance hit)
 full: Wait for GPU to finish (accurate but slow, GPU-CPU sync stall)
 none: Disable readback completely (some games render better without it)

readback_memexport.name: readback_memexport
readback_memexport.description: Read data written by memory export in shaders on the CPU. This may be needed in some games (but many only access exported data on the GPU, and this flag isn't needed to handle such behavior), but causes mid-frame synchronization, so it has a huge performance impact.

force_convert_triangle_fans_to_lists.name: force_convert_triangle_fans_to_lists
force_convert_triangle_fans_to_lists.description: For host graphics API downlevel support testing only, force CPU conversion of triangle fans to triangle lists even if the host supports triangle fan primitives natively.

force_convert_line_loops_to_strips.name: force_convert_line_loops_to_strips
force_convert_line_loops_to_strips.description: For host graphics API downlevel support testing only, force CPU conversion of line loops to line strips even if the host supports line loop primitives natively.

force_convert_quad_lists_to_triangle_lis.name: force_convert_quad_lists_to_triangle_lists
force_convert_quad_lists_to_triangle_lis.description:
For host graphics API downlevel support testing only, force CPU conversion of quad lists to quad strips even if the host supports quad list primitives natively or via geometry shader emulation.
May also be useful for graphics debugging when the debugger doesn't display the geometry generated by geometry shaders properly.

convert_16bit_list_indices_to_32bit_on_m.name: convert_16bit_list_indices_to_32bit_on_metal
convert_16bit_list_indices_to_32bit_on_m.description:
On hosts that cannot disable primitive restart (Metal/MoltenVK), widen 16-bit primitive-reset-disabled index buffers that actually use 0xFFFF as a real vertex index to 32-bit, so 0xFFFF (-> 0x0000FFFF) is not misinterpreted as a primitive restart and the primitive is not dropped. Default on: the pipeline forces primitiveRestartEnable for strip/fan topologies on these hosts (Metal cannot disable it), so this widening is the correctness safeguard for the max-index-as-real-vertex case.
Disable only to confirm the symptom (geometry partially vanishing / flickering on Metal); has no effect on other backends (gated on the host being unable to disable primitive restart).

moltenvk_draw_diagnostics.name: moltenvk_draw_diagnostics
moltenvk_draw_diagnostics.description: Temporary G1 diagnostics for hosts that cannot disable primitive restart (Metal/MoltenVK): for every indexed draw, log a once-per-signature line with the topology, index format, endian, primitive-reset state, processing path, and whether a maximum index value (0xFFFF 16-bit / 0xFFFFFFFF 32-bit) present in the guest buffer reaches the host draw unprotected (would be eaten by Metal's always-on primitive restart). Scans every indexed draw's guest buffer - diagnostic use only.

ignore_32bit_vertex_index_support.name: ignore_32bit_vertex_index_support
ignore_32bit_vertex_index_support.description: For host graphics API downlevel testing only (useful only for Qualcomm Adreno 4xx-level host GPU testing), force indirection or pre-masking and pre-swapping of 32-bit vertex indices as if the host only supports 24-bit indices.

primitive_processor_cache_min_indices.name: primitive_processor_cache_min_indices
primitive_processor_cache_min_indices.description:
Smallest number of guest indices to store in the cache to try reusing later in the same frame if processing (such as primitive type conversion or reset index replacement) is performed.
Setting this to a very high value may result in excessive CPU processing, while a very low value may result in excessive locking and lookups.
Negative values disable caching.

trace_gpu_prefix.name: trace_gpu_prefix
trace_gpu_prefix.description: Prefix path for GPU trace files.

trace_gpu_frame_at_swap.name: trace_gpu_frame_at_swap
trace_gpu_frame_at_swap.description: Capture a single-frame GPU trace (like the Trace Frame hotkey) when the swap counter reaches this value. 0 disables. For unattended captures where no UI hotkey is available.

trace_gpu_frame_repeat_interval.name: trace_gpu_frame_repeat_interval
trace_gpu_frame_repeat_interval.description: With trace_gpu_frame_at_swap, capture another single-frame trace every this many swap-counter ticks after the first (0 = one capture only). For catching intermittent frames.

trace_gpu_frame_repeat_count.name: trace_gpu_frame_repeat_count
trace_gpu_frame_repeat_count.description: Total single-frame traces trace_gpu_frame_repeat_interval captures, the first included.

dump_shaders.name: dump_shaders
dump_shaders.description: For shader debugging, path to dump GPU shaders to as they are compiled.

framerate_limit.name: framerate_limit
framerate_limit.description:
Maximum frames per second. 0 = Unlimited frames.
Defaults to 60, when set to 0, and VSYNC is enabled.

gpu_allow_invalid_fetch_constants.name: gpu_allow_invalid_fetch_constants
gpu_allow_invalid_fetch_constants.description: Allow texture and vertex fetch constants with invalid type - generally unsafe because the constant may contain completely invalid values, but may be used to bypass fetch constant type errors in certain games until the real reason why they're invalid is found.

gpu_allow_invalid_upload_range.name: gpu_allow_invalid_upload_range
gpu_allow_invalid_upload_range.description: Allows games to read data from pages that are marked as no access.

non_seamless_cube_map.name: non_seamless_cube_map
non_seamless_cube_map.description: Disable filtering between cube map faces near edges where possible (Vulkan with VK_EXT_non_seamless_cube_map) to reproduce the Direct3D 9 behavior.

half_pixel_offset.name: half_pixel_offset
half_pixel_offset.description: Enable support of vertex half-pixel offset (D3D9 PA_SU_VTX_CNTL PIX_CENTER). Generally games are aware of the half-pixel offset, and having this enabled is the correct behavior (disabling this may significantly break post-processing in some games), but in certain games it might have been ignored, resulting in slight blurriness of UI textures, for instance, when they are read between texels rather than at texel centers, or the leftmost/topmost pixels may not be fully covered when MSAA is used with fullscreen passes.

occlusion_query_fake_lower_threshold.name: occlusion_query_fake_lower_threshold
occlusion_query_fake_lower_threshold.description:
Lower end of the fake sample count value written on EVENT_WRITE_ZPD when real occlusion queries are disabled.
-1 writes nothing, resulting in some games that sit and hang.
0 means the fake result stays fully occluded.

occlusion_query_fake_upper_threshold.name: occlusion_query_fake_upper_threshold
occlusion_query_fake_upper_threshold.description:
Upper end of the fake sample count value written on EVENT_WRITE_ZPD when real occlusion queries are disabled.
Keep this higher than occlusion_query_fake_lower_threshold.
Ignored if occlusion_query_fake_lower_threshold is -1.

occlusion_query_querybatch_range.name: occlusion_query_querybatch_range
occlusion_query_querybatch_range.description:
Range of fake sample count values to walk for titles using the D3D QueryBatch standard before wrapping back to occlusion_query_fake_lower_threshold.
This shouldn't be changed from the default value of 0 (disabled) unless necessary for a specific title.

occlusion_query_saturation.name: occlusion_query_saturation
occlusion_query_saturation.description:
Compress higher occlusion query sample counts before guest writeback.
This can be useful if effects such as lens flares appear too strong.
1.0 = default behavior
0.0 = collapse all nonzero sample counts to 1
Values around 0.90 are a good starting point for subtle tuning.

anisotropic_override.name: anisotropic_override
anisotropic_override.description:
Forces anisotropic filtering (AF) for eligible textures.
Higher values keep textures sharper at oblique angles at the cost of GPU bandwidth, though most GPUs handle up to 16x fine.
In rare cases, forcing AF can introduce visual artifacts.
 -1 = No override
  0 = Disable anisotropic filtering
  1 = Force 1x anisotropic filtering
  2 = Force 2x anisotropic filtering
  3 = Force 4x anisotropic filtering
  4 = Force 8x anisotropic filtering
  5 = Force 16x anisotropic filtering

no_discard_stencil_in_transfer_pipelines.name: no_discard_stencil_in_transfer_pipelines
no_discard_stencil_in_transfer_pipelines.description: Skip stencil bit discard in render target transfer pipelines. May improve performance on some GPUs.

gpu_3d_to_2d_texture.name: gpu_3d_to_2d_texture
gpu_3d_to_2d_texture.description: Handle shaders that sample 3D textures as 2D by creating a 2D texture from slice 0 of the guest memory.

async_shader_compilation.name: async_shader_compilation
async_shader_compilation.description: Compile shaders and create pipelines asynchronously in background threads. Eliminates shader compilation stutter but may cause brief rendering artifacts while pipelines are being created. When disabled, pipelines are created synchronously which causes stutter but no visual artifacts.

ac6_ground_fix.name: ac6_ground_fix
ac6_ground_fix.description: This fixes(hide) issues with black ground in AC6. Use only in AC6. Might cause issues in other titles.

depth_float24_sample_z_varying.name: depth_float24_sample_z_varying
depth_float24_sample_z_varying.description: With depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader: pass the NDC depth (z/w) from the vertex shader as a sample-interpolated noperspective varying and convert that instead of gl_FragCoord.z - the exact per-sample depth even on hosts where FragCoord.z is not per-sample under sample-rate shading (Apple GPUs via MoltenVK), without the precision loss of the derivative-based reconstruction at steep triangles. Takes precedence over depth_float24_sample_z_from_derivatives.

depth_float24_sample_z_from_derivatives.name: depth_float24_sample_z_from_derivatives
depth_float24_sample_z_from_derivatives.description: With depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader: reconstruct the per-sample depth as z + dFdx(z)*dx + dFdy(z)*dy from the sample position instead of trusting gl_FragCoord.z, for hosts where FragCoord.z is not evaluated at the sample position under forced sample-rate shading (Apple GPUs via MoltenVK: sample pairs receive identical depth, which neutralizes Z-prepasses and flattens MSAA depth).

texture_alpha_test_lod_snap.name: texture_alpha_test_lod_snap
texture_alpha_test_lod_snap.description: For draws with the fixed-function alpha test enabled, snap the shader-computed/register texture LOD to the nearest integer mip. Alpha-tested fragment survival flips on the filtered alpha crossing the reference, so sampler-internal cross-vendor differences (blend weight precision, ramp shape) directly flip fragment ownership at triangle edges (the Apple-vs-AMD/Xenos mesh); single-level sampling makes the verdict host-invariant. Requires texture_computed_lod_in_shader for computed-LOD fetch coverage.

texture_decompress_bc.name: texture_decompress_bc
texture_decompress_bc.description: Decompress BC1/BC2/BC3 (DXT) textures to RGBA8 at upload with Xenia's own compute shaders instead of sampling the compressed blocks - the hardware BC decoders' interpolation precision is vendor-specific (notably the BC3/DXT5 3-bit interpolated alpha), which flips alpha-test verdicts at threshold-adjacent pixels across GPUs.

texture_trilinear_ramp_match_amd.name: texture_trilinear_ramp_match_amd
texture_trilinear_ramp_match_amd.description: Remap the explicit-LOD trilinear blend fraction to the AMD/Xenos ramp (weight = saturate((frac - 0.1) / 0.8), measured; Apple GPUs use a plain linear ramp) - reproduces AMD's mip pair and blend weight including the pure-level dead zones within 0.1 of integer LODs. Applies to register-LOD and shader-computed-LOD fetches (combine with texture_computed_lod_in_shader for coverage of computed-LOD fetches).

texture_mip_lod_bias_adjust.name: texture_mip_lod_bias_adjust
texture_mip_lod_bias_adjust.description: Constant sampler mipLodBias applied to all guest texture samplers, calibrating the host GPU's lambda->mip-pair mapping to the Xenos/AMD convention (Apple GPUs transition ~0.099 LOD later than AMD at identical explicit LOD - the cross-GPU triangle-edge mesh). Default 0.0 (neutral); the 0.099 Apple calibration is opt-in and applied only on the texture-determinism host (Apple, or force-enabled), inert elsewhere.

interpolators_manual_perspective.name: interpolators_manual_perspective
interpolators_manual_perspective.description: Interpolate guest interpolators as noperspective A = o/w (vertex shader pre-divides by the final position W) and reconstruct o = A / gl_FragCoord.w in the fragment shader prologue. Quad derivatives of perspective-interpolated varyings at partially covered quads are implementation-defined and differ between Apple and AMD GPUs (up to ~1000x at edge pixels - the cross-GPU wireframe mesh via texture LOD); noperspective varyings and gl_FragCoord are helper-lane-exact on both vendors, making values AND derivatives host-invariant.

texture_computed_lod_in_shader.name: texture_computed_lod_in_shader
texture_computed_lod_in_shader.description: Convert texture gradients to a scalar LOD with a host-invariant formula in the shader (1D/2D fetches with computed LOD) instead of passing Grad operands - the hardware gradients-to-LOD function is implementation-defined and flat-triangle-constant, so cross-GPU formula differences flip whole triangles to adjacent mips (the Apple-vs-AMD wireframe mesh on high-contrast art). Disables anisotropic filtering for the converted fetches.

texture_lod_primitive_id_analytic_interp.name: texture_lod_primitive_id_analytic_interp
texture_lod_primitive_id_analytic_interp.description: See texture_lod_primitive_id_analytic: source interpolator index whose .xy carries the fetch's uv (specimen ground PS: 0).

texture_lod_primitive_id_analytic.name: texture_lod_primitive_id_analytic
texture_lod_primitive_id_analytic.description: EXPERIMENTAL / research only - not a shipping rendering path. Enabling it allocates a 256 MiB device ring and adds a per-vertex SSBO write plus per-fragment index/SSBO loads; it fixes only the narrow desert/character- seam LOD-scatter and is not calibrated for general content. Apple analytic per-triangle texture-LOD gradient sourced via gl_PrimitiveID + the per-vertex SSBO (no PerVertexKHR / MoltenVK fork). The VS writes {A=uv/w, W=1/w, ndc.xy} per vertex; the PS reads its triangle's three vertices by primitive-id and computes a per-triangle-constant (plane-exact) LOD, removing the per-quad LOD scatter that dashes the ground on non-plane-exact Apple interpolation. fix-apple-lod-primitive-id-analytic-gradient.

texture_lod_primitive_id_analytic_tf.name: texture_lod_primitive_id_analytic_tf
texture_lod_primitive_id_analytic_tf.description: See texture_lod_primitive_id_analytic: fetch-constant index to apply the primitive-id analytic LOD to (-1 = all).

texture_determinism_force_non_apple.name: texture_determinism_force_non_apple
texture_determinism_force_non_apple.description: Diagnostic: treat non-Apple GPUs as a texture-determinism host so the individually-enabled stack cvars (texture_computed_lod_in_shader, interpolators_manual_perspective, texture_alpha_test_lod_snap, texture_mip_lod_bias_adjust) also take effect off Apple, for symmetric cross-vendor A/B experiments. The stack defaults OFF everywhere (opt-in); this only widens the host gate, it does not enable any layer on its own.

texture_lod_covered_lane_inputs.name: texture_lod_covered_lane_inputs
texture_lod_covered_lane_inputs.description: With texture_computed_lod_in_shader + interpolators_manual_perspective: before quad-differencing the analytic-LOD inputs, replace each helper (uncovered) lane's value with the first covered lane's value in the 2x2 quad. Helper-lane values are only cross-vendor equal to ~ulp, and the quotient rule catastrophically cancels at edge-on triangles, amplifying that noise into multi-mip LOD differences at partially covered quads (Apple-vs-AMD alpha-test ownership flips - the mesh). Quad coverage itself is cross-vendor identical, so the corrected lambda is host-invariant; fully covered quads are unaffected.

texture_lod_force_level.name: texture_lod_force_level
texture_lod_force_level.description: Diagnostic: pin all guest texture samplers to this exact mip level (minLod = maxLod = N). Comparing single-level renders across GPUs separates mip content / BC-decode divergence from LOD selection divergence. -1 = off.

apple_texture_lod_force_base.name: apple_texture_lod_force_base
apple_texture_lod_force_base.description: On Apple GPUs, pin texture sampling to the base mip (level 0) by default. Apple's per-triangle quad-derivative LOD diverges across triangle edges, producing a mip-seam "crosshatch" net on character skin in many titles (USF4/RDR/TMNT). Pinning the base mip removes it at near-zero cost - much cheaper than the in-shader analytic LOD - trading mip minification (some distant-texture shimmer) for clean surfaces, which suits close-camera content. Applied only on Apple hosts. An explicit texture_lod_force_level >= 0 overrides this; set this false to restore normal mip selection on Apple.

force_per_sample_shading_probe.name: force_per_sample_shading_probe
force_per_sample_shading_probe.description: Diagnostic: add a SampleId input to all translated pixel shaders, forcing per-sample shading without any depth conversion - isolates the shading-rate side effect of depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader from its depth quantization math.

ps_debug_export_instr.name: ps_debug_export_instr
ps_debug_export_instr.description: Diagnostic, with ps_debug_export_ps_hash: ucode instruction slot index (the number shown in ucode disassembly) after which the register selected by ps_debug_export_reg is captured in the matching pixel shader; the captured value replaces guest color output 0 at the end of the shader, so intermediate ALU dataflow can be read back through the render target. -1 = off.

ps_debug_export_reg.name: ps_debug_export_reg
ps_debug_export_reg.description: See ps_debug_export_instr: index of the temporary register (rN) to capture.

ps_debug_export_lod.name: ps_debug_export_lod
ps_debug_export_lod.description: Diagnostic, with ps_debug_export_ps_hash: capture the shader-computed analytic texture LOD of the matching pixel shader's computed-LOD fetches into guest color output 0 (readback through the render target). 1 = R:max texel-gradient magnitude/32, G:lambda/16+0.5, B:helper-neighbor fraction of the 2x2 quad; 2 = R:axis-X gradient/32, G:axis-Y gradient/32, B:lambda/16+0.5; 3 = analytic-vs-hardware de-risk: R:analytic lambda/16+0.5, G:hardware OpImageQueryLod lambda/16+0.5, B:(analytic-hardware)/16+0.5 (same coords/GPU -> isolates whether the analytic FORMULA reproduces hardware LOD); 4 = plane-exactness walk (uses ps_debug_export_scale as gain): R:q(=inv_w)*scale, G:0.5+scale*d(q)/dx, B:0.5+scale*d(o)/dx where o=A/q is the reconstructed perspective UV -> shows whether the ballooning UV finite difference is inherited from the denominator q (G scatters) or appears only in o (numerator A not plane-exact). Isolates whether the Apple analytic-LOD collapse is a gradient magnitude loss and which axis loses it; 5 = exact-bits export: pack the full IEEE-754 word of the quantity selected by ps_debug_export_bits into RGBA8 (byte 0->R .. byte 3->A, each value/255) so the interpolated value can be compared bit-exact cross-machine / used offline (untile, reassemble uint, bitcast to float). -1 = off.

ps_debug_export_bits.name: ps_debug_export_bits
ps_debug_export_bits.description: See ps_debug_export_lod=5: which quantity to bit-pack. 0=A.x (o.x*W), 1=A.y, 2=W(=1/w), 3=o.x (reconstructed UV), 4=o.y.

ps_debug_export_lod_tf.name: ps_debug_export_lod_tf
ps_debug_export_lod_tf.description: See ps_debug_export_lod: restrict the LOD capture to the fetch whose texture fetch-constant index equals this value (a pixel shader samples several textures with different gradients; without this the last fetch wins). -1 = capture every computed-LOD fetch (last stored wins).

ps_debug_export_lod_range.name: ps_debug_export_lod_range
ps_debug_export_lod_range.description: See ps_debug_export_lod: half-range (in mips) of the lambda encoding. Encoded value E = lambda/(2*range) + 0.5, so lambda in [-range,+range] maps to [0,1]. Default 8 matches the historical /16 scale; widen (e.g. 16) to see whether horizon LODs genuinely agree or are merely clamped at the +8 ceiling.

ps_debug_export_ps_hash.name: ps_debug_export_ps_hash
ps_debug_export_ps_hash.description: See ps_debug_export_instr: hex ucode hash of the pixel shader to instrument (required - empty disables the export).

ps_debug_export_scale.name: ps_debug_export_scale
ps_debug_export_scale.description: See ps_debug_export_instr: multiplier applied to the captured register before it is written to color output 0, for reading values much smaller than the render target's LSB.

ps_debug_export_component.name: ps_debug_export_component
ps_debug_export_component.description: See ps_debug_export_instr: -1 = export the register as-is; 0-3 = broadcast that component (x/y/z/w) to RGB, making the w component readable through the color output.

mulsc_round_toward_zero.name: mulsc_round_toward_zero
mulsc_round_toward_zero.description: Round mulsc products toward zero instead of to nearest even. This fixes bad geometry in several Volition Engine titles and possibly others. This rounding behavior hasn't been confirmed on real hardware, so it's disabled by default.

point_sampling_extra_offset.name: point_sampling_extra_offset
point_sampling_extra_offset.description: Extra texel-space offset added to point-sampled (nearest-neighbor) texture fetch coordinates, in texels. Point-sampled fetches with explicit half-texel instruction offsets (such as manual PCF shadow sampling) land exactly on texel boundaries, where the rounding convention is implementation-defined and differs between GPUs (the Xenos nearest_clamp_policy convention; Apple GPUs pick the opposite neighbor to AMD/NVIDIA at exact ties, producing dark self-shadowing lines along triangle edges - the cross-title "wireframe mesh"). A small positive value (e.g. 0.03125 = 1/32 texel) makes the selection deterministic and consistent with the desktop convention. Applied only when both the magnification and minification filters are point.

resolve_resolution_scale_fill_half_pixel.name: resolve_resolution_scale_fill_half_pixel_offset
resolve_resolution_scale_fill_half_pixel.description: When using resolution scaling, apply the hack that stretches the first surely covered host pixel in the left and top sides of render target resolve areas to eliminate the gap caused by the half-pixel offset (this is necessary for certain games to display the scene graphics).

use_fuzzy_alpha_epsilon.name: use_fuzzy_alpha_epsilon
use_fuzzy_alpha_epsilon.description: Use approximate compare for alpha values to prevent flickering on NVIDIA graphics cards

dxbc_switch.name: dxbc_switch
dxbc_switch.description: Use switch rather than if for flow control. Turning this off or on may improve stability, though this heavily depends on the driver - on AMD, it's recommended to have this set to true, as some titles appear to crash when if is used for flow control (possibly the shader compiler tries to flatten them). On Intel HD Graphics, this is ignored because of a crash with the switch instruction.

dxbc_source_map.name: dxbc_source_map
dxbc_source_map.description: Disassemble Xenos instructions as comments in the resulting DXBC for debugging.

metal_stencil_export.name: metal_stencil_export
metal_stencil_export.description: Rebuild depth/stencil render targets from EDRAM in one pass, writing the stencil value from the shader, instead of one depth pass plus eight stencil bit-plane passes. Performance only (Just Cause 2 +15% on an M4); turn off only to troubleshoot a rendering problem. XE_METAL_STENCIL_EXPORT=0/1 overrides this setting.

metal_raster_sync_skip.name: metal_raster_sync_skip
metal_raster_sync_skip.description: Skip re-synchronizing a render target with EDRAM when nothing has changed since its last synchronization. Performance only (Just Cause 2 +12% on an M4); turn off only to troubleshoot a rendering problem. XE_METAL_RASTER_SYNC_SKIP=0/1 overrides this setting.

metal_raster_mark_skip.name: metal_raster_mark_skip
metal_raster_mark_skip.description: Skip re-marking EDRAM tiles a render target already owns on every draw. Performance only (Just Cause 2 +5% on an M4); turn off only to troubleshoot a rendering problem. XE_METAL_RASTER_MARK_SKIP=0/1 overrides this setting.

metal_resolve_span_coalesce.name: metal_resolve_span_coalesce
metal_resolve_span_coalesce.description: Synchronize a full-width resolve's EDRAM rows as one span instead of row by row. Performance only (Just Cause 2 +25% on an M4 once the other optimizations are on); turn off only to troubleshoot a rendering problem. XE_METAL_RESOLVE_SPAN_COALESCE=0/1 overrides this setting.

metal_present_format_convert.name: metal_present_format_convert
metal_present_format_convert.description: When the selected swap source's pixel format differs from the guest output format, convert it per-channel instead of replicating the red channel. Enabled by default: the red-replication path was a debug visualization that a real title reaches -- Halo 3 presents an RGBA16Float source for every swap, and its guest image is fully chromatic, so it was being flattened to grey. Set false to restore the previous output exactly.

metal_pass_attachments_by_use.name: metal_pass_attachments_by_use
metal_pass_attachments_by_use.description: Bind a Metal draw pass's colour, depth and stencil attachments only when a draw in the pass can read or write them, so the Apple GPU skips the tile load and store of untouched attachments (mostly the stencil plane of passes that never test stencil). The set is learned per pass so pass boundaries stay where they were; attachment contents are unchanged. Promoted 2026-10-03 (Just Cause 2 at 2x2 draw scale 10.5 -> 10.8 fps on an M4, corpus identical). XE_METAL_PASS_ATTACHMENTS=0/1 overrides this setting; XE_METAL_PASS_ATTACHMENTS_LEGACY=1 forces the bind-everything policy.

metal_memexport_raster_mode.name: metal_memexport_raster_mode
metal_memexport_raster_mode.description: Experimental: route memory exports from vertex shaders that also rasterize (the exports of a draw that has a render target bound). Required by titles that copy data through such draws, for example Child of Eden's video decoder; costs about 13% more GPU submissions per frame on Viva Pinata. auto: only for titles that set metal_memexport_raster (their built-in config). on: every title. off: none. XE_METAL_MEMEXPORT_RASTER=0/1 overrides.

metal_msaa_clear_fold.name: metal_msaa_clear_fold
metal_msaa_clear_fold.description: Draw the Xbox 360's 2x/4x MSAA fast clears straight into the matching 1x view of the same EDRAM instead of copying the whole surface out and back for each clear. Large speedup in titles that clear MSAA buffers often (Gears of War 3: 18 -> 30 fps on an M4); no visual change is intended - clears it cannot prove identical take the old path. Turn off only to troubleshoot a rendering problem. XE_METAL_MSAA_CLEAR_FOLD=0/1 overrides this setting.

metal_unwritten_interpolators.name: metal_unwritten_interpolators
metal_unwritten_interpolators.description: What a pixel shader reads from an interpolator its vertex shader never wrote, for draws whose vertex shader writes none (a position-only quad drawn with a leftover pixel shader). The Xbox 360 leaves the value undefined. off: zero, as the reference renderer does. on: 0.5, which fixes Resident Evil 5's flickering shadows but changes Halo 3's lighting. auto: 0.5 only for titles whose built-in config sets metal_unwritten_interpolators_title.

metal_completion_wait.name: metal_completion_wait
metal_completion_wait.description: Wait for the GPU to finish pending resolves before the guest sees a completion signal (interrupt or end-of-pipe event), instead of only submitting them. Fixes Mass Effect's one-frame colour wrap on the Earth shot, but stops the CPU and GPU from overlapping, which cost most titles a third of their frame rate (Red Dead Redemption 27 -> 12 fps on an M1 Max). auto: only for titles whose built-in config sets metal_completion_wait_title. on: every title. off: none. XE_METAL_EXPOSURE_WAIT=0/1 overrides.

metal_texture_integer_scale.name: metal_texture_integer_scale
metal_texture_integer_scale.description: Restore the guest's integer range for texture fetches whose fetch constant declares an integer num_format on a fixed-point format. The host view samples normalized, so without this the guest receives [0, 1] where it asked for unnormalized units. Enabled by default: Just Cause 2 fetches a per-texel light/material index table this way and truncates the result into the address register, so normalized delivery collapsed every index to 0 and pinned the whole per-texel selection to one constant. Also carries the rest of upstream's fixed texture conversion: unsigned-biased components decode as offset binary (an 8-bit 128 returns 0), normalized unsigned components round to 16 fractional bits, and point sampled fetches snap to texel centers and reconstruct 4 to 7 bit components. Set false to restore the behavior before any of these exactly.

metal_guest_gamma_ramp.name: metal_guest_gamma_ramp
metal_guest_gamma_ramp.description: Apply the guest's standard 256-entry gamma ramp to the presented guest output on Metal. Enabled by default: five calibrated titles program a complete non-identity ramp that is present at every swap, and ignoring it presented an untransformed image. Set false to restore the previous output exactly -- no ramp buffer is created, no upload occurs, and the swap source reaches the mailbox by the same blit as before.

metal_pwl_gamma.name: metal_pwl_gamma
metal_pwl_gamma.description: Apply the guest's piecewise-linear gamma ramp when DC_LUTA_CONTROL selects it (value 3, an 8-step increment over a 10-bit input; Halo 3). false presents those titles without a ramp, the pre-2026-10-10 behavior.

metal_pipeline_metallib_cache.name: metal_pipeline_metallib_cache
metal_pipeline_metallib_cache.description: Persist translated metallib across runs so a warm launch does not re-translate what a previous run already translated. Removes 95-96% of measured translation cost on a warm launch. Set to false for the exact rollback: no durable reads or writes.

metal_pipeline_binary_archive.name: metal_pipeline_binary_archive
metal_pipeline_binary_archive.description: Persist host pipeline state in an MTLBinaryArchive (M2). Addresses the 1.7-47.5% the census attributed to newRenderPipelineState. Default off until gated.

metal_pipeline_cache_title_cap_mib.name: metal_pipeline_cache_title_cap_mib
metal_pipeline_cache_title_cap_mib.description: Maximum durable Metal pipeline-cache size per title, in MiB. On reaching it, no NEW artifacts are admitted for the session; existing entries keep being used.

metal_pipeline_cache_global_cap_mib.name: metal_pipeline_cache_global_cap_mib
metal_pipeline_cache_global_cap_mib.description: Maximum total durable Metal pipeline-cache size across all titles, in MiB. Enforced between sessions by evicting whole least-recently-used title directories.

metal_dxil_cache.name: metal_dxil_cache
metal_dxil_cache.description: Persist the DXBC->DXIL intermediate in a store keyed only on what DXIL depends on (libdxilconv, converter options, converter generation). A RESILIENT INTERMEDIATE cache, not a warm-start one: it does nothing on an ordinary warm launch, where the metallib store already serves. It earns its place by surviving changes that legitimately invalidate every metallib - an OS update, a Metal Shader Converter upgrade, a different GPU, a shader-ABI bump - so dxilconv is not re-paid (measured: 295 ms Sonic, 584 ms Just Cause 2), and by deduplicating byte-identical DXBC within a cold run. Set to false for the exact rollback: no durable DXIL reads or writes.

metal_dxil_cache_verify_every_nth.name: metal_dxil_cache_verify_every_nth
metal_dxil_cache_verify_every_nth.description: Sampled DXIL cache-hit verification: every Nth hit is compared byte-for-byte against a fresh conversion, and a mismatch drops the entry and uses the fresh bytes. 0 disables sampling. This is the behavioral backstop for a key that cannot see a behavior nobody knew had changed; each sampled hit costs one conversion, which is the cost the cache exists to avoid.

metal_dxil_cache_cap_mib.name: metal_dxil_cache_cap_mib
metal_dxil_cache_cap_mib.description: Maximum durable DXIL artifact-store size in MiB. On reaching it no NEW artifacts are admitted for the session; existing ones keep being served.

texture_host_dump.name: texture_host_dump
texture_host_dump.description: Diagnostic: hex guest base address of a texture whose CONVERTED host buffer contents (output of the texture load compute shader, before the copy to the host image) are read back and written to texhost_<base>_<seq>.bin in the current directory at shutdown. For cross-host comparison of loaded texture content.

texture_host_dump_image.name: texture_host_dump_image
texture_host_dump_image.description: Diagnostic: hex guest base address of a texture whose HOST IMAGE contents (read back with vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer immediately after the buffer-to-image copy at load) are written to texhostimg_<base>_<seq>.bin in the current directory at shutdown, in the same buffer layout as --texture_host_dump (bytes outside the copied level rectangles are zero-filled). A texhost_ vs texhostimg_ difference on one machine convicts the buffer-to-image copy path; identical contents exonerate it and implicate the image view/sampler.

texture_host_dump_sample.name: texture_host_dump_sample
texture_host_dump_sample.description: Diagnostic, requires --texture_host_dump_image with the same value: hex guest base address of a texture whose base level is additionally read back through the SHADER SAMPLING path - a y-flipped nearest-filter vkCmdBlitImage into a temporary image (MoltenVK implements flipped blits by rendering with the source bound as a sampled texture, bypassing this app's descriptors), then a transfer readback of the temporary image, written to texhostsmp_<base>_<seq>.bin (base level only, tightly packed, rows bottom-up). Differing from texhostimg_ means shader reads of the texture disagree with transfer reads at the Metal level.

render_target_path_vulkan.name: render_target_path_vulkan
render_target_path_vulkan.description:
Render target emulation path to use on Vulkan.
Use: [any, fbo, fsi]
 fbo:
  Host framebuffers and fixed-function blending and depth / stencil testing, copying between render targets when needed.
  Lower accuracy (limited pixel format support).
  Performance limited primarily by render target layout changes requiring copying, but generally higher.
 fsi:
  Manual pixel packing, blending and depth / stencil testing, with free render target layout changes.
  Requires a GPU supporting fragment shader interlock.
  Highest accuracy (all pixel formats handled in software).
  Performance limited primarily by overdraw.
 Any other value:
  Choose what is considered the most optimal for the system (currently always FB because the FSI path is much slower now).

vulkan_sparse_shared_memory.name: vulkan_sparse_shared_memory
vulkan_sparse_shared_memory.description: Enable sparse binding for shared memory emulation. Disabling it increases video memory usage - a 512 MB buffer is created - but allows graphics debuggers that don't support sparse binding to work.

moltenvk_disable_centroid_interpolation.name: moltenvk_disable_centroid_interpolation
moltenvk_disable_centroid_interpolation.description: Temporary G1 diagnostic: force all pixel shader interpolators to center (never centroid) sampling. Centroid interpolation only differs from center on partially-covered MSAA edge pixels; if the dark edge-line mesh disappears with this set, MoltenVK/Metal centroid handling at MSAA edge pixels is the source. Diagnostic use only - center sampling can cause texture bleeding at polygon edges the guest avoided via centroid.

depth_only_fragment_shader.name: depth_only_fragment_shader
depth_only_fragment_shader.description: Attach a minimal empty fragment shader to depth/stencil-only guest pipelines instead of omitting the fragment stage entirely. Probe for Apple-GPU depth interpolation divergence between fragment-less (depth-only fast path) and full pipelines, which breaks EQUAL-class depth tests of Z-prepassed geometry (fix-apple-gpu-raster-cracks).

moltenvk_force_primitive_restart.name: moltenvk_force_primitive_restart
moltenvk_force_primitive_restart.description: On MoltenVK, create strip/fan pipelines with primitiveRestartEnable forced on to match Metal's always-enabled primitive restart. Disable only for G1 diagnosis (A/B of the 681935cc3 force-on): MoltenVK will warn per strip pipeline, and some MoltenVK versions may fail pipeline creation (historically observed as a DOA5 round-load stall).

vulkan_pipeline_creation_threads.name: vulkan_pipeline_creation_threads
vulkan_pipeline_creation_threads.description: Number of threads used for graphics pipeline creation. -1 to calculate automatically (75% of logical CPU cores), a positive number to specify the number of threads explicitly (up to the number of logical CPU cores), 0 to disable multithreaded pipeline creation.

depth_bias_extra.name: depth_bias_extra
depth_bias_extra.description: Extra host depth bias constant factor (in minimal-resolvable-depth units, i.e. Vulkan depthBiasConstantFactor) added to every guest draw with a depth attachment on the host render target path. Biasing fragment depth slightly towards the viewer (positive, with the Xbox 360's inverted depth range) makes GREATER_EQUAL depth tests of multi-pass geometry robust against sub-24-bit fixed-function depth interpolation differences between the passes' pipelines - on Apple GPUs these differences otherwise produce dark triangle-edge lines (the cross-title "wireframe mesh"). 16 = about two 20e4 depth ULPs.

moltenvk_skip_rectangle_draws.name: moltenvk_skip_rectangle_draws
moltenvk_skip_rectangle_draws.description: Temporary G1 diagnostic: skip all draws that use the rectangle-list-as-triangle-strip vertex shader expansion (the geometry-shader-less MoltenVK path). If the wireframe overlay disappears while this is set, the rectangle expansion is the source. Breaks fullscreen passes / UI compositing while enabled - diagnostic use only.

fullscreen.description: Whether to launch the emulator in fullscreen.

controller_hotkeys.description: Hotkeys for Xbox and PS controllers.

disabled_controller_hotkeys.description: Comma-separated controller-hotkey function ids the user has disabled (managed by the Controllers UI).

dashboard_sounds_asked.name: dashboard_sounds_asked
dashboard_sounds_asked.description: Whether the dashboard has offered to download its sounds. They are not included with the app.

dashboard_freezes_game.name: dashboard_freezes_game
dashboard_freezes_game.description: Freeze the running game while the dashboard is open, so nothing happens in it until you go back.

show_fps.name: show_fps
show_fps.description: Show the frame rate in a corner of the window while a game runs.

preferences_key.name: preferences_key
preferences_key.description: Keyboard key that opens and closes Preferences: F6, F7, F8, F10 or none. Command-comma always works.

preferences_button.name: preferences_button
preferences_button.description: Controller button that opens Preferences: guide (a tap of Guide on its own), back_start (Back and Start together) or none.

postprocess_scaling_and_sharpening.name: postprocess_scaling_and_sharpening
postprocess_scaling_and_sharpening.description:
Post-processing effect to use for resampling and/or sharpening of the final display output.
Use: [bilinear, cas, fsr, metalfx]
 bilinear (or any value not listed here):
  Original image at 1:1, simple bilinear stretching for resampling.
 cas:
  Use AMD FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening (CAS) for sharpening at scaling factors of up to 2x2, with additional bilinear stretching for larger factors.
 fsr:
  Use AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 (FSR) for highest-quality upscaling, or AMD FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening for sharpening while not scaling or downsampling.
  For scaling by factors of more than 2x2, multiple FSR passes are done.
 metalfx:
  Use Apple MetalFX spatial upscaling, in one pass at any factor (Metal renderer only; bilinear elsewhere).

postprocess_ffx_cas_additional_sharpness.name: postprocess_ffx_cas_additional_sharpness
postprocess_ffx_cas_additional_sharpness.description:
Additional sharpness for AMD FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening (CAS), from 0 to 1.
Higher is sharper.

postprocess_ffx_fsr_max_upsampling_passe.name: postprocess_ffx_fsr_max_upsampling_passes
postprocess_ffx_fsr_max_upsampling_passe.description:
Maximum number of upsampling passes performed in AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 (FSR) before falling back to bilinear stretching after the final pass.
Each pass upscales only to up to 2x2 the previous size. If the game outputs a 1280x720 image, 1 pass will upscale it to up to 2560x1440 (below 4K), after 2 passes it will be upscaled to a maximum of 5120x2880 (including 3840x2160 for 4K), and so on.
This variable has no effect if the display resolution isn't very high, but may be reduced on resolutions like 4K or 8K in case the performance impact of multiple FSR upsampling passes is too high, or if softer edges are desired.
The default value is the maximum internally supported by Xenia.

postprocess_ffx_fsr_sharpness_reduction.name: postprocess_ffx_fsr_sharpness_reduction
postprocess_ffx_fsr_sharpness_reduction.description:
Sharpness reduction for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 (FSR), in stops.
Lower is sharper.

postprocess_dither.name: postprocess_dither
postprocess_dither.description:
Dither the final image output from the internal precision to 8 bits per channel so gradients are smoother.
On a 10bpc display, the lower 2 bits will still be kept, but noise will be added to them - disabling may be recommended for 10bpc, but it depends on the 10bpc displaying capabilities of the actual display used.

recent_titles_entry_amount.name: recent_titles_entry_amount
recent_titles_entry_amount.description: How many recently played titles the File menu lists. Every title played is kept for the dashboard's All Games list; 0 keeps none.

screenshot_path.name: screenshot_path
screenshot_path.description: Folder for screenshots (F12 and screenshot_interval). Empty: a screenshots folder beside the executable.

screenshot_interval.name: screenshot_interval
screenshot_interval.description: Seconds between automatic screenshots of the guest output, for unattended test runs (no screen-recording permission needed). 0 = off.

screenshot_interval_ms.name: screenshot_interval_ms
screenshot_interval_ms.description: Milliseconds between automatic screenshots, overriding screenshot_interval when > 0 (burst capture for flicker hunts). Burst filenames carry a sequence number and the guest swap count. 0 = off.

log_fps_interval.name: log_fps_interval
log_fps_interval.description: Seconds between GuestFps log lines (guest swaps per second, any GPU backend), for unattended test runs. 0 = off.

disable_doubleclick_fullscreen.name: disable_doubleclick_fullscreen
disable_doubleclick_fullscreen.description: Allows the user to disable the behavior where a fast double-click causes Xenia to enter fullscreen mode.

hid.name: hid
hid.description: Input system. Use: [any, nop, sdl, winkey, xinput]

storage_root.name: storage_root
storage_root.description: Root path for persistent internal data storage (config, etc.), or empty to use the path preferred for the OS, such as the documents folder, or the emulator executable directory if portable.txt is present in it.

content_root.name: content_root
content_root.description: Root path for guest content storage (saves, etc.), or empty to use the content folder under the storage root.

cache_root.name: cache_root
cache_root.description: Root path for files used to speed up certain parts of the emulator or the game. These files may be persistent, but they can be deleted without major side effects such as progress loss. If empty, the cache folder under the storage root, or, if available, the cache directory preferred for the OS, will be used.

install_root.name: install_root
install_root.description: Root path for games' hard drive installs (the console's cache drives, cache0, cache1 and cache), or empty to use the storage root. Relative paths are under the storage root.

load_module_map.name: load_module_map
load_module_map.description: Loads a .map for symbol names and to diff with the generated symbol database.

dump_ppc_functions.name: dump_ppc_functions
dump_ppc_functions.description: Comma-separated hex guest addresses (e.g. 8233CFA0,826E8BE8); log the PPC source disassembly of matching functions when they are generated. For classifying PC-sampler hotspots.

trace_function_coverage.name: trace_function_coverage
trace_function_coverage.description: Generate tracing for function instruction coverage statistics.

trace_function_references.name: trace_function_references
trace_function_references.description: Generate tracing for function address references.

trace_function_data.name: trace_function_data
trace_function_data.description: Generate tracing for function result data.

validate_hir.name: validate_hir
validate_hir.description: Perform validation checks on the HIR during compilation.

pvr.name: pvr
pvr.description:
Known PVR's.
 0x710200 = Used by Zephyr 
 0x710300 = Used by Zephyr
 0x710500 = Used by Jasper
 0x710700 = Default
 0x710800 = Used by Corona V1 & V2
Processor version and revision number.
Bits 0 to 15 are the version number.
Bits 16 to 31 are the revision number.
Note: Some XEXs (such as mfgbootlauncher.xex) may check for a value that's less than 0x710700.

break_on_instruction.name: break_on_instruction
break_on_instruction.description: int3 before the given guest address is executed.

disable_instruction_infocache.description: Disables caching records of called instructions/mmio accesses.

writable_code_segments.name: writable_code_segments
writable_code_segments.description: Enables a program to write to its own code segments in memory.

enable_early_precompilation.name: enable_early_precompilation
enable_early_precompilation.description: Enable pre-compiling guest functions that we know we've called/that we've recognized as being functions via simple heuristics, good for error finding/stress testing with the JIT

debug.name: debug
debug.description: Allow debugging and retain debug information.

trace_function_data_path.name: trace_function_data_path
trace_function_data_path.description: File to write trace data to.

break_on_start.name: break_on_start
break_on_start.description: Break into the debugger on startup.

disable_prefetch_and_cachecontrol.name: disable_prefetch_and_cachecontrol
disable_prefetch_and_cachecontrol.description: Disables translating ppc prefetch/cache flush instructions to host prefetch/cacheflush instructions. This may improve performance as these instructions were written with the Xbox 360's cache in mind, and modern processors do their own automatic prefetching.

no_reserved_ops.name: no_reserved_ops
no_reserved_ops.description: For testing whether a game may have races with a broken reserved load/store impl

disable_context_promotion.name: disable_context_promotion
disable_context_promotion.description: Disables Context Promotion optimizations, this may be needed for some sports games, but will reduce performance.

ignore_trap_instructions.name: ignore_trap_instructions
ignore_trap_instructions.description: Generate no code for powerpc trap instructions, can result in better performance in games that aggressively check with trap.

break_on_unimplemented_instructions.name: break_on_unimplemented_instructions
break_on_unimplemented_instructions.description: Break to the host debugger (or crash if no debugger attached) if an unimplemented PowerPC instruction is encountered.

elide_e0_check.name: elide_e0_check
elide_e0_check.description: Eliminate e0 check on some memory accesses, like to r13(tls) or r1(sp)

enable_rmw_context_merging.name: enable_rmw_context_merging
enable_rmw_context_merging.description: Permit merging read-modify-write HIR instr sequences together into x86 instructions that use a memory operand.

debugprint_trap_log.name: debugprint_trap_log
debugprint_trap_log.description: Log debugprint traps to the active debugger

ignore_undefined_externs.name: ignore_undefined_externs
ignore_undefined_externs.description: Don't exit when an undefined extern is called.

emit_source_annotations.name: emit_source_annotations
emit_source_annotations.description: Add extra movs and nops to make disassembly easier to read.

enable_incorrect_roundingmode_behavior.name: enable_incorrect_roundingmode_behavior
enable_incorrect_roundingmode_behavior.description: Disables the FPU/VMX MXCSR sharing workaround, potentially causing incorrect rounding behavior and denormal handling in VMX code. The workaround may cause reduced CPU performance but is a more accurate emulation

align_all_basic_blocks.name: align_all_basic_blocks
align_all_basic_blocks.description: Aligns the start of all basic blocks to N bytes. Only specify a power of 2, 16 is the recommended value. Results in larger icache usage, but potentially faster loops

instrument_call_times.name: instrument_call_times
instrument_call_times.description: Compute time taken for functions, for profiling guest code
